This is the method of how air and fuel are introduced to the engine, typically naturally aspirated, turbo (single or multiple), supercharging or twincharging (turbo with supercharger).
Layout of the cylinders within an engine, typically configured in a straight line (in-line) or a V.
Number of combustion chambers in an internal combustion engine.
The Camshaft is an internal component of a vehicle's engine that provides the correct timings for the valves to take in fuel and expel gasses from the engine.
A more efficient engine will typically have more valves per cylinder (typically 4).
Higher performance engines typically have higher compression ratios as there will be more force in each stroke from the piston in the cylinder, creating more power.

This relates to the rotational force or 'strength' of a vehicle's engine, measured in Newton metres (Nm). Depending on the car, this could mean either more speed or more pulling/load carrying capability.

This is calculated by dividing the vehicle's engine power by the vehicle's weight, expressed as kilowatt per tonne (kW/t).

Vehicles are rated in half star increments based upon the vehicle’s tailpipe carbon dioxide (CO2) emissions released per kilometre. Only vehicles with no tail pipe emissions achieve a 6-star rating. VESR is a star rating developed by NSW Government that has been applied to light passenger vehicles sold on the Australian market since 2004.
This is the level of Euro emission standards (up to Euro 6) that the vehicle complies with. The higher the number, the more environmentally friendly.
This is the type of steering on a vehicle e.g. rack and pinion, 4 wheel steering etc.
The material of a vehicle's wheel, either steel or alloy.
This is the size of a front wheel of a vehicle e.g. 16 inch, 16 x 7. This can show measurements for both wheel diameter and width.
This is the size of a rear wheel of a vehicle e.g. 16 inch, 16 x 7. This can show measurements for both wheel diameter and width.
This describes the width of the tyre in mm, the thickness of the wall of the tyre (profile), the construction type (usually radial), and the diameter of the tyre in inches.
This describes the width of the tyre in mm, the thickness of the wall of the tyre (profile), the construction type (usually radial), and the diameter of the tyre in inches.
Length of a vehicle at its longest point.
Width of a vehicle at its widest point (excluding mirrors).
Height of a vehicle at its highest point.
The distance between the centre of the front wheels and and the centre of the rear wheels.
The distance between a vehicle's front wheels taken from the centre of the tyres.
The distance between a vehicle's rear wheels taken from the centre of the tyres.
The total weight of a vehicle with standard equipment, no occupants and 10 litres of fuel.
Total weight of a vehicle with standard equipment, no occupants and a full tank of fuel.
This is the maximum weight of the vehicle including all occupants and any luggage.
The weight that can be carried by a vehicle while driving. This may include occupants and luggage, but does not include any towing.
The towing capacity of the car if the trailer has its own braking system. Anything over 750kg is required to have brakes independent of the car's brakes.
The towing capacity of the car if the trailer does not have brakes.  Anything under 750kg is not required to have brakes independent of the car's brakes.
